title: Homemade Banana Pancakes
excerpt: On sleepy mornings, the sweet smell of pancakes turning golden in the skillet can bring everyone to the kitchen, just like it did at Grandma’s house. These tender banana pancakes are made with ripe fruit, a little cinnamon, and plenty of cozy homemade goodness for a breakfast worth lingering over.

Why You'll Love These Homemade Banana Pancakes

  • Ripe bananas bring natural sweetness and tender texture to every bite.
  • A little cinnamon makes the kitchen smell wonderfully cozy while they cook.
  • The batter comes together with simple pantry staples in just a few minutes.
  • These banana pancakes are soft, golden, and just right for a relaxed family breakfast.
  • They are easy to customize with your favorite wholesome toppings.

Ingredients

Gather these simple ingredients for a stack of tender banana pancakes with plenty of old-fashioned homemade flavor.

  • Ripe bananas – 2, peeled
  • Large egg – 1
  • Milk – 3/4 cup
  • Unsalted butter – 2 tablespoons, melted, plus extra for the skillet
  • All-purpose flour – 1 1/2 cups
  • Brown sugar – 2 tablespoons
  • Baking powder – 1 1/2 teaspoons
  • Baking soda – 1/2 teaspoon
  • Ground cinnamon – 1/2 teaspoon
  • Salt – 1/4 teaspoon
  • Maple syrup – for serving

How to Make Homemade Banana Pancakes

Plan for 10 minutes of prep and about 20 minutes of cooking. The batter rests for 5 minutes, giving the ingredients a moment to come together before the pancakes hit the skillet.

Step 1: Mash the Bananas

Place the peeled bananas in a medium mixing bowl. Mash them with a fork until mostly smooth, leaving a few small pieces for a bit of extra banana flavor.

Step 2: Add the Egg and Milk

Whisk the egg and milk into the mashed bananas until the mixture is evenly combined. A few soft banana streaks are perfectly fine.

Step 3: Stir in the Butter

Whisk the melted butter into the banana mixture. Make sure the butter is warm rather than hot so it blends smoothly.

Step 4: Combine the Dry Ingredients

In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. This helps distribute the leavening and spices throughout the batter.

Step 5: Mix the Batter

Stir the banana mixture into the dry ingredients until just combined. Do not overmix; a few small lumps will help keep the pancakes tender.

Step 6: Rest the Batter

Let the batter rest for 5 minutes. This short pause allows the flour to hydrate and helps the pancakes cook up soft and fluffy.

Step 7: Heat the Skillet

Heat a lightly greased skillet over medium-low heat. The gentler heat gives the pancakes time to cook through without browning too quickly.

Step 8: Portion the Pancakes

Pour 1/4 cup of batter onto the skillet for each pancake, leaving enough room between them to flip easily. Cook in batches if needed.

Step 9: Cook the First Side

Cook the pancakes until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set. This usually takes a few minutes, depending on the skillet and heat.

Step 10: Flip and Finish

Flip the pancakes carefully and cook until the second side is golden brown. Transfer finished pancakes to a plate while you cook the remaining batter.

Step 11: Serve Warm

Serve the pancakes warm with maple syrup. Add your favorite toppings if desired, and enjoy them while they are soft and fresh.

Pro Tips for Making Homemade Banana Pancakes

  • Use bananas with plenty of brown spots for the sweetest flavor and softest texture.
  • Measure the flour by spooning it into a measuring cup and leveling the top for lighter pancakes.
  • Keep the skillet over medium-low heat so the centers cook before the outsides become too dark.
  • Grease the skillet lightly between batches, wiping away any excess butter if it begins to brown.
  • Mix only until the dry ingredients disappear to avoid dense pancakes.

How to Serve Homemade Banana Pancakes

  • Drizzle warm pancakes with maple syrup and add a pat of butter.
  • Top them with sliced bananas, berries, or a sprinkle of cinnamon.
  • Serve with yogurt for a creamy contrast and a little extra staying power.
  • Add chopped nuts for a gentle crunch, if your family enjoys them.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing Leftovers

  • Let leftover pancakes cool completely before placing them in an airtight container.
  • Refrigerate for up to 3 days, separating layers with parchment or wax paper if desired.

Freezing

  • Arrange cooled pancakes in a single layer on a tray and freeze until firm.
  • Transfer them to a freezer-safe container or bag, placing parchment between layers.
  • Freeze for up to 2 months for the best texture and flavor.

Reheating

  • Warm refrigerated or frozen pancakes in a toaster, toaster oven, or skillet until heated through.
  • For a larger batch, place them on a baking sheet and warm gently until soft and hot.
  • Serve right away with maple syrup.

Final Thoughts

These homemade banana pancakes are a sweet, simple way to make an ordinary morning feel a little more special.

FAQs

Here are a few helpful answers for making a lovely stack of banana pancakes at home.

Can I use very ripe bananas?

Yes. Very ripe bananas with brown spots are ideal because they add extra sweetness and mash easily.

Why are my banana pancakes dense?

Dense pancakes usually come from overmixing the batter or using too much flour. Stir just until the ingredients are combined and measure the flour carefully.

Can I make the batter ahead of time?

For the best texture, cook the batter soon after its 5-minute rest. You can prepare the dry and wet mixtures separately ahead of time, then combine them just before cooking.

How do I keep the pancakes warm while cooking?

Place cooked pancakes on a plate and cover them loosely while you finish the batch. Avoid stacking too tightly if you want the edges to stay pleasantly tender.
